cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The Highway Transportation System is the connected _____ of roads, streets and highways used by public and private traffic.
cards.back: The Highway Transportation System is the connected network of roads, streets and highways used by public and private traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The transportation system aims to move people and goods safely, efficiently and promptly while protecting the _____ .
cards.back: The transportation system aims to move people and goods safely, efficiently and promptly while protecting the environment.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Every road user shares _____ for following the system’s rules and cooperating with others.
cards.back: Every road user shares responsibility for following the system’s rules and cooperating with others.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The road _____ supports ordinary trips, deliveries and emergency responses.
cards.back: The road network supports ordinary trips, deliveries and emergency responses.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The system’s people component includes drivers, passengers, pedestrians, road workers, police, emergency personnel and _____ at play.
cards.back: The system’s people component includes drivers, passengers, pedestrians, road workers, police, emergency personnel and children at play.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Vehicles sharing the system range from passenger cars and _____ to buses, trucks, farm vehicles and emergency vehicles.
cards.back: Vehicles sharing the system range from passenger cars and bicycles to buses, trucks, farm vehicles and emergency vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The roads component includes _____ , United States, state and county routes, along with toll roads and parkways.
cards.back: The roads component includes Interstate, United States, state and county routes, along with toll roads and parkways.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The transportation _____ makes personal travel, work, school, shopping and recreation possible.
cards.back: The transportation network makes personal travel, work, school, shopping and recreation possible.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ manufacturing, highway construction, freight movement, travel and vehicle repair are economic activities supported by the road system.
cards.back: Vehicle manufacturing, highway construction, freight movement, travel and vehicle repair are economic activities supported by the road system.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: OMV manages licensing and vehicle-related matters such as plates, registration, _____ and titles.
cards.back: OMV manages licensing and vehicle-related matters such as plates, registration, fees and titles.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Police, highway patrol and sheriff’s departments contribute to safe travel through _____ .
cards.back: Police, highway patrol and sheriff’s departments contribute to safe travel through enforcement.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Traffic courts support _____ of traffic law.
cards.back: Traffic courts support enforcement of traffic law.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Highway engineering improves the road system, while _____ engineering improves vehicle safety and operation.
cards.back: Highway engineering improves the road system, while vehicle engineering improves vehicle safety and operation.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Emergency responders and trauma centers work to reduce collision _____ during the emergency and afterward.
cards.back: Emergency responders and trauma centers work to reduce collision losses during the emergency and afterward.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Public education prepares road users through knowledge of traffic rules, _____ -operation skills and attitudes consistent with safety.
cards.back: Public education prepares road users through knowledge of traffic rules, vehicle-operation skills and attitudes consistent with safety.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Collisions can impose personal _____ as well as financial costs for wages, medical care, rehabilitation, services and property damage.
cards.back: Collisions can impose personal losses as well as financial costs for wages, medical care, rehabilitation, services and property damage.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Traffic-safety comparisons can use collision and death counts relative to the _____ .
cards.back: Traffic-safety comparisons can use collision and death counts relative to the distance traveled.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide’s dated Louisiana fatality-cause list identifies alcohol, _____ , aggressive behavior and missing seat-belt use.
cards.back: The guide’s dated Louisiana fatality-cause list identifies alcohol, distraction, aggressive behavior and missing seat-belt use.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Drivers, pedestrians and bicyclists may have different _____ and viewpoints when they share the transportation system.
cards.back: Drivers, pedestrians and bicyclists may have different needs and viewpoints when they share the transportation system.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A driver needs to anticipate mistakes and _____ actions by other road users.
cards.back: A driver needs to anticipate mistakes and unsafe actions by other road users.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Different vehicle types have different _____ , braking, speed-control and performance capabilities.
cards.back: Different vehicle types have different steering, braking, speed-control and performance capabilities.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A vehicle’s equipment, _____ , condition and maintenance affect its handling.
cards.back: A vehicle’s equipment, age, condition and maintenance affect its handling.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Understanding the capabilities of trucks or motorcycles matters even to a driver who _____ operates those vehicles.
cards.back: Understanding the capabilities of trucks or motorcycles matters even to a driver who never operates those vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ speeds create hazards, particularly on freeways and expressways.
cards.back: Unsafe speeds create hazards, particularly on freeways and expressways.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Driving below the posted limit can still be too fast for the weather, traffic or the _____ ’s physical condition.
cards.back: Driving below the posted limit can still be too fast for the weather, traffic or the driver’s physical condition.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Highway design takes expected traffic volume and _____ mix into account when choosing lanes, shoulders and medians.
cards.back: Highway design takes expected traffic volume and vehicle mix into account when choosing lanes, shoulders and medians.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A _____ road is maintained and regulated by its parish.
cards.back: A parish road is maintained and regulated by its parish.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A _____ highway is regulated by the state.
cards.back: A state highway is regulated by the state.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide describes United States highways as a route system that predates the _____ program.
cards.back: The guide describes United States highways as a route system that predates the Interstate program.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ highways carry large traffic volumes on routes across the country.
cards.back: Interstate highways carry large traffic volumes on routes across the country.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide associates even-numbered _____ routes with east–west travel and odd-numbered routes with north–south travel.
cards.back: The guide associates even-numbered Interstate routes with east–west travel and odd-numbered routes with north–south travel.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide describes an expressway as a divided high-volume highway with at least _____ lanes.
cards.back: The guide describes an expressway as a divided high-volume highway with at least four lanes.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Freeway is another term the guide uses for an _____ .
cards.back: Freeway is another term the guide uses for an expressway.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A toll road collects a _____ for use, which may involve a ticket or prepaid pass.
cards.back: A toll road collects a charge for use, which may involve a ticket or prepaid pass.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide describes a _____ as a divided highway with substantial surrounding trees or other landscaping.
cards.back: The guide describes a parkway as a divided highway with substantial surrounding trees or other landscaping.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: On a divided highway, a _____ or barrier separates traffic moving in opposing directions.
cards.back: On a divided highway, a median or barrier separates traffic moving in opposing directions.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A limited-access highway permits entry and exit at _____ signed locations.
cards.back: A limited-access highway permits entry and exit at designated signed locations.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide describes partial access as allowing connections at other streets while _____ driveways and other direct access.
cards.back: The guide describes partial access as allowing connections at other streets while excluding driveways and other direct access.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide contrasts _____ access with other roads that permit street or driveway connections.
cards.back: The guide contrasts exit-only access with other roads that permit street or driveway connections.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Wider shoulders and gentler curves and grades are road-design measures intended to _____ collisions.
cards.back: Wider shoulders and gentler curves and grades are road-design measures intended to reduce collisions.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Reducing roadside obstacles can lessen injury severity when a _____ leaves the roadway.
cards.back: Reducing roadside obstacles can lessen injury severity when a vehicle leaves the roadway.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Sound pavement helps tires maintain _____ and supports quicker stopping.
cards.back: Sound pavement helps tires maintain grip and supports quicker stopping.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Poorly maintained roads may present _____ , ruts and shoulder drop-offs that create driving hazards.
cards.back: Poorly maintained roads may present potholes, ruts and shoulder drop-offs that create driving hazards.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Rain, including a light drizzle, can reduce tire _____ on the road.
cards.back: Rain, including a light drizzle, can reduce tire grip on the road.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Hydroplaning occurs when tires skim on accumulated _____ instead of gripping the roadway.
cards.back: Hydroplaning occurs when tires skim on accumulated water instead of gripping the roadway.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Road drainage is designed to move water _____ from the driving surface.
cards.back: Road drainage is designed to move water away from the driving surface.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Grooves and rough pavement texture help tires retain traction and _____ skidding.
cards.back: Grooves and rough pavement texture help tires retain traction and reduce skidding.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Electronic or dynamic message signs can warn of hazards such as _____ , strong winds or ice.
cards.back: Electronic or dynamic message signs can warn of hazards such as fog, strong winds or ice.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: In _____ y areas, roads may include space beside the roadway for snow pushed aside by plows.
cards.back: In snowy areas, roads may include space beside the roadway for snow pushed aside by plows.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The _____ works on roadway safety, public education and reducing highway deaths.
cards.back: The Federal Highway Administration works on roadway safety, public education and reducing highway deaths.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Signs, traffic signals and _____ -of-way controls direct actions and stopping at intersections.
cards.back: Signs, traffic signals and right-of-way controls direct actions and stopping at intersections.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Traffic-control devices communicate through their _____ , shapes and displayed information.
cards.back: Traffic-control devices communicate through their colors, shapes and displayed information.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ signs and pavement markings help drivers see guidance at night.
cards.back: Reflective signs and pavement markings help drivers see guidance at night.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Breakaway poles, guardrails, skid-resistant pavement and all-weather markings can reduce _____ severity.
cards.back: Breakaway poles, guardrails, skid-resistant pavement and all-weather markings can reduce collision severity.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Rumble strips warn a _____ that the vehicle is leaving the road or moving toward another lane.
cards.back: Rumble strips warn a driver that the vehicle is leaving the road or moving toward another lane.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Dedicated turn lanes, roundabouts and coordinated signals are measures used to _____ intersection crashes.
cards.back: Dedicated turn lanes, roundabouts and coordinated signals are measures used to reduce intersection crashes.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A driver’s _____ extends to passengers, other drivers, pedestrians and other people’s property.
cards.back: A driver’s responsibility extends to passengers, other drivers, pedestrians and other people’s property.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ road sharing requires obeying traffic law and treating other users with the consideration the driver would want in return.
cards.back: Safe road sharing requires obeying traffic law and treating other users with the consideration the driver would want in return.
